03 / CHECK THE PREDICTION

Hide a test. Predict it. Compare.

Each experiment is left out once. A new model uses the other four to predict the hidden result. The table shows every comparison for the quantity selected above.

Hidden testDiameter (mm)ReportedPredictedDifferenceWithin remaining sizes?

This is an internal check on five experiments, not independent validation. The two endpoint tests fall outside the size range of their four training tests and are labelled. Small sample size, nearby droplet sizes, mixed flights and varying drift limit what the error can establish. The error is not a confidence interval or a safety margin.

Equations, assumptions and training tests

Burn duration uses initial diameter squared as its input; overall K uses diameter directly. Each fit minimises squared differences from the reported values. The diameter-squared relationship motivates a simple model; it does not turn the regression into a full combustion simulation.

A separate baseline predicts the average of the other four outcomes. Comparing with this baseline helps reveal when a fitted trend adds little information. The 20% oxygen cases, approximate diameters and incomplete measurements remain in the dataset, with their exclusion reasons.

05 / FOLLOW THE NUMBERS

Source, extraction and method.

From the report to this page

  1. Preserve NASA’s original PDF and record its SHA-256 checksum.
  2. Extract Table 1 into structured cells. Retain the printed value beside every parsed number.
  3. Compare all 38 rows of pressure, atmosphere, initial diameter, burn duration and overall K with a separate visual transcription of the rendered pages.
  4. Keep other columns and their original cells available for inspection. Fit only the checked model inputs and outputs.

NASA record ↗ · Original Table 1, PDF pp. 21–22 ↗

Source and extraction checked 15 November 2026. The NASA record and report agree on investigation identity and the 38-test scope. Table 1 summaries are imported; instrument recordings and calibration files are not.

Read the values correctly

Pressure and atmosphere are test conditions. Diameters and duration are reported from imaging. K is the report’s derived rate of change of squared diameter. It is not a directly measured speed.

Per-cell uncertainty for burn duration and K is not given in Table 1. Approximate diameter estimates keep their original ± values. Air is labelled “Air”; its oxygen fraction has not been filled in from an assumption.
